During the [[Age of Legends]], many different types of life were created using the [[One Power|Power]] and technology. The creation of such '''constructs''' was overseen by a strict code of ethics, which made genetic alteration on living creatures above the level of plants illegal. For some unknown reason, most constructs are incapable of passing through [[Traveling#Gateways|gateways]], making weaves such as [[Deathgates]] effective weapons against them.

=Known constructs=
==Shadowspawn==
{{main|Shadowspawn}}
[[Shadowspawn]] were originally created in the [[Age of Legends]] by the Forsaken [[Aginor]] to serve the [[Shadow]]. A leading geneticist, Aginor went over to the Shadow because he wished to experiment outside the code of ethics - though the promise of immortality was also part of the reason - and the resulting creatures were dubbed Shadowspawn. Unlike other constructs, they were universally evil, because they were made using the taint of the [[Dark One]]. Those marked as [[Chosen]] were to be obeyed absolutely by all sentient{{ref|"Dumb animal" Shadowspawn such as [[Stick|Sticks]] and possibly [[Jumara (Shadowspawn)|Jumara]] are not shown to obey orders from anyone and may not be capable of doing so.}}<!--Maybe there's a better word than "sentient." It's debatable whether Draghkar or Zomara would be considered "sentient," but they clearly follow orders.--> Shadowspawn.

Direct Shadowspawn constructs include [[Gray Men]], ''[[Gholam]]'', and arguably [[Slayer]]. Other Shadowspawn were initially constructed, but are capable of reproduction and propagation. These include [[Trolloc|Trollocs]], [[Myrddraal]], and [[Draghkar]], along with the various creatures of the [[Great Blight]], including [[Jumara (Shadowspawn)|Jumara]], [[Stick|Sticks]], etc. The existence (or lack thereof) of reproduction among some other Shadowspawn, such as [[Zomaran]], is ambiguous.

==Nym==
The [[Nym]] are constructs of Aes Sedai from the Age of Legends, with the ability to use the One Power for the benefit of agriculture.{{ref/book|twotc|Nym}} They looked like humanoid plant creatures with hazelnuts  for eyes and shoots for hair. They tended the massive farms and gardens of the Age of Legends and worked alongside the [[Ogier]] and the [[Da'shain Aiel]] during [[Song of Growing#Seed Singing|Seed Singing]]. Proportionally, they were as much taller than Ogier as Ogier were than men. 

It was said that a Nym would not die as long as plants grew{{ref/book|12|26}} and that “Where a Nym touched, all manner of green and growing things thrived”.{{ref/book|bwb|3}} Most of the Nym were killed during the War of the Shadow. [[Someshta]] was one of the last of the Nym, given the task to watch the [[Eye of the World]] by ancient Aes Sedai. When he died, he took [[Balthamel]] with him. A massive oak tree spontaneously grew from Someshta's grave.  

The head of a Nym remained alive in a cave in [[Shara]], but it was killed by [[Demandred]] when he was searching for the last piece of the ''sa'angreal'' [[Sakarnen]].

Nym are sometimes referred to as [[Treebrother|Treebrothers]].{{ref/book|1|49}}{{ref/book|1|53}}

==Chora trees==
{{main|chora}}
Chora trees lined the streets of the cities of the [[Age of Legends]]. They are distinguished by their tri-foil leaves and the feeling of contentment a person gets when under one's branches. All chora trees except one were destroyed during the Breaking of the World, and that one was planted in the center of [[Rhuidean]]. The tree was known to the rest of the world as ''[[Avendesora]]'', and the [[Aiel]] seemingly knew how to tend it. [[Avendoraldera]] was a cutting from ''Avendesora'', given to the [[Cairhien]]in as repayment for the gift of water to the [[Aiel]] clans. It represented the promise of free travel through the [[Aiel Waste]] to the lands of [[Shara]]. It was destroyed in the event known as [[Laman's Pride]], when he cut down the tree to make himself a throne (see the [[Aiel War]]).

There were rumors that the nation of [[Almoth Plain|Almoth]] also possessed a living sapling of Avendesora, or at least a branch, but have so far been unsubstantiated.

The keys to opening a [[Waygate]] are also in the shape of a chora leaf.
